description_text:
The USS Enterprise CV-6 was the second unit of the Yorktown class, being laid down in 1934, launched in 1936 and being commissioned in 1938. She featured a sizeable airwing, capable crew and good speed, allowing her to fight more effectively than other classes.
When the Imperial Japanese Navy attacked the US and thus forced them to enter WW2, it was the task of the three Yorktowns to keep the Pacific under the control of the US. Enterprise saw heavy combat in the Coral Sea, yet her hardest fight would come at Midway. Within that battle she sank three enemy carriers, a record which couldnt be beaten until today. Even though her two sisterships were lost, the situation had been improved for the US.
Until the end of the war, Enterprise would become the most famoust and highest decorated vessel of any Navy, another record which couldnt be beaten. Once the war was over, attempts were made to keep her as a museum ship, which all failed. CV-6 was scrapped in 1960, her name given to CVN-65. Since CVN-65 has been decomissioned in 2012, the next carrier bearing the name of Enterprise will be CVN-80, planned to enter service in the 2030s.
Note: This model is recommended to be used in the 1/4000 scale. The model itself isnt scaled, the scale table is down below.
1/4000: 6,25cm or 2.46in
1/3000: 8,3cm or 3.27in
1/2000: 12,5cm or 4.92in  (not recommended)
For self calculation: The Enterprise was 251 metres or 824 ft 9 in long
The model is intended to be used with little supports as possible, yet some are recommended around the main island and the overhangs of the deck on bow and stern. The level of detail is more than mixed in this model, some parts may not be printed at all. I recommend using a resin printer for this, with supports placed under fragile parts like the cranes and individual decks. Up and Downsclaling might be possible, yet I dont know to what extend.
If you have ideas for more ships to model, feel free to message me.

Polygon saving but accurate 3d model created according to real reference. Native format is a blender, model can use Hypernurbs subdivision. Other formats are exported in one resolution. Exported formats Blender, fbx, and obj are prepared well to work correctly with every standard modeling software such as Maya, Lightwave, etc... Using FBX file for import is strongly recommended because it preserves basic material properties, objects hierarchy, uvw coordinates, and quad geometry. 3ds format preserves basic material properties, hierarchy, and uvw coordinates, but all geometry is triangular.OBJ format preserves only quad geometry and uvw coordinates. Each format of model (except for OBJ) has a hierarchy of parents and children objects ready to animate manually or using any car animation plugin. All mesh parts separated by material are jointed under one empty (no polygons) object used as their pivot. All materials, textures, and objects are sorted well to make Your own materials for special render engines. Previews were rendered using Blender, a Physical renderer. Model scale unit is centimeters. Environment scene where the car is placed is not included! Description:The Arado Ar 196 was a shipboard reconnaissance low-wing monoplane aircraft built by the German firm of Arado starting in 1936. The next year it was selected as the winner of a design contest and became the standard aircraft of the Kriegsmarine (German Navy) throughout World War II.In 1933, the Kriegsmarine looked for a standardized shipboard observation floatplane. After a brief selection period, the Reichsluftfahrtministerium (German Air Ministry, RLM) decided on the Heinkel He 60 biplane. This was one of a line of developments of a basic biplane airframe that appeared as a number of floatplanes, trainers, and fighters. Deliveries started in a matter of months.The plane proved to have only slightly better performance than the He 60, and its sea-handling was poor. Rushed modifications resulted in a series of nine prototypes in an attempt to solve some of the problems, but they did not help much. The Navy gave up, and the planes were eventually sold off to Romania, Spain and Sweden.

description_text:
The Yamato-class of battleships was the largest class of ships ever built. No battleship since has been as large, with other nations not coming even close to the displacement of the class. Three units were built in total: Yamato, Musashi and Shinano, all prior and during the second world war.
Since Japans industry was smaller than the ones of other nations, they couldnt build as many ships in several classes like the US did at the time. Hence a class of giant dimensions was planned, even though they would violate several treaties and agreements. Still the ships were built, having a displacement of up to 71.000 tons, bearing a main calibre of 18.1". Two ships, the Yamato and Musashi were completed as designed, yet Shinano was converted into a carrier during the war after the loss at Midway.
Musashi would see no use against other battleships during the war. Her main task was to house the commanding officers of the naval forces, gaining the nickname of a Hotel in the process. Her biggest and last mission would happen in Leyte Gulf, the biggest naval battle of the Pacific campaign. She was attacked by several aircraft carriers at once, being unable to shoot down the many planes in the sky. After taking 19 torpedoes and 17 bombs, she finally went under, taking the majority of the crew with her. That left only Yamato as the operational battleship of the class. The battle of Leyte Gulf ended in a defeat of the Japanese forces, having lost many important units to hold up the advancing US troops.

The model is intended to be used with little supports as possible, yet some are recommended around the barrels, below the secondary platforms, the rangefinders and the cage mast aft. I recommend using a resin printer for this, with supports placed under fragile parts like the barrels. Up and downscaling might be possible, yet I dont know to what extend.

description_text:
The Haskell-class of transport ships were designed and built during the second world war by the US. Their design was based on the Victory-class of merchant ships which were constructed to combat the high losses of merchants in both threatres. Their main task was to carry landing ships and their troops to islands where they would then be unloaded. 117 units were built, with some of them serving in Korea and even Vietnam. The last few units were scrapped in the early 2000s.
Due to the high amount of troops oboard and the high number, these ships proved to be highly effective in capturing the many islands which Imperial Japan held. Since they could be anchored offshore and support the troops from far away, there was little the ground forces could do against them. However, several ships were hit by kamikazes, resulting in sometimes great damage. Once the war was over, most units were used in operation Magic Carpet, where the soldiers were transported back to the US. Most units were then mothballed in 1946.

description_text:
The Doris Miller is a supercarrier of the Gerald R Ford class, planned to be built in the late 2020s. Being a successor of the already proven and highly capable Nimitz-class, this carrier is designed to be the standard type of aircraft carrier built for the navy in the coming decades. Having entered service in 2017, the Gerald R Ford is the newest and most advanced airfract carrier in active duty, carrying the most modern systems and aircraft. Doris Miller is named after an afro-american hero of the US Navy, having been awarded the Navy cross after the attack on Pearl Harbor. 
Overall the characteristics are similar to the Nimitz class, meaning that the carrier uses nuclear propulsion with practically endless range. The tonnage and speed are also quite similar, yet the amount of aircraft carrier has decreased slightly. However, the ship requires almost 700 less personnel to operate fully, thanks to automation and heavy usage of computers. The overall dimensions have also changed not much, yet more capable radar and computing systems have been integrated into the ship, proofing it for the projected 40 year long service life. Noteworthy is, that during the construction of this class, the Navy tries to eliminate paper usage as much as possible. Future units are already being built with that concept, allowing more quicker alterations during the building process and quicker assembly times.
Doris Miller will replace the Carl Vinson in 2032 and is planned to be laid down within the next few years, being the fourth ship of the class. More units are planned yet unnamed for the time being. With the current crisis in the world, plans have been made to accelerate the building process by building Enterprise and Doris Miller in the same dock, as possible. Due to that reason, an earlier completion date is likely.
Note: This model is recommended to be used in the 1/4000 scale. The model itself isnt scaled, the scale table is down below.
1/5000: 6,6cm or 2.59
1/4000: 8,3cm or 3.26in
1/3000: 11,1cm or 4.37in
For self calculation: The Gerald R Ford class is roughly 333m or 1092ft long.
The model is intended to be used with little supports as possible, yet some are recommended below the bow at a large scale. I recommend using a resin printer for this, otherwise important details might be lost. Up and Downscaling might be possible, yet I dont know to what extend.
If you face issues with the model, have questions or want to propose some changes, please reach out to me, I am always happy to help. I am also open for suggetions for new ships which I havent done yet, as I am looking to expand my catalogue of ships.

Its GRAU designation was 4K40, its NATO reporting name was Styx or SS-N-2. China acquired the design in 1958 and created at least four versions: the CSS-N-1 Scrubbrush and CSS-N-2 versions were developed for ship-launched operation, while the CSS-C-2 Silkworm and CSS-C-3 Seersucker were used for coastal defence. Other names for this basic type of missile include: HY-1, SY-1, and FL-1 Flying Dragon (Chinese designations typically differ for export and domestic use, even for otherwise identical equipment), North Korean local produced KN-1 or KN-01, derived from both Silkworm variants and Russian & USSR P-15, Rubezh, P-20 P-22 .

description_text:
Arihant-class is a class of nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine designed and built indigenously by India. It holds a distinction of being the only class of SSBNs, designed and operated by a nation which is not a permanent member of UNSC. First two boats of the class, namely INS Arihant and INS Arighaat have a displacement of 6000 tons and are capable of carrying four K-4 SLBMs while the third boat, INS Aridhaman displaces 7000 tons and can carry up to eight K-4 SLBMs.
Here, 1/200 scale model of Arihant-class submarines is provided. As an easter egg, this model is completely free for downloaders!!! Don't forget to add comments and share pictures when you 3d-print this model. Following files are provided:

  - 
INS Arihant/Arighaat model without masts: The model is same for both INS Arihant and INS Arighaat.

  - 
INS Aridhaman model without masts: This model is provided in two variants (in two separate files), in first variant, all missile silos are grouped at the center of the hump, while in second variant, the missile silos are grouped in two separate groups.

  - 
The model of masts: Masts are identical for all the models.

  - Guide model for placement of masts and propeller at correct positions. This model is not recommended for printing since the thin masts may not come out well and may break. One may also consider using metal wire in place of very thin pieces on masts. Just cut-out the thin part, drill a hole in its place, glue a straight piece of wire in its place, carefully keeping the length of the mast.

  - Right-handed and Left-Handed propellers (in separate files). Either of them can be used with the submarine. Glue a 4mm rod into the slot provided in the propeller hub. And insert the other end (preferably after applying some lube oil) into the long slot provided in the submarine hull.

This is highly detailed model and can also be used at larger scales (e.g. 1/72 or 1/48). At larger scales the panel lines on the hull might be a bit too heavily pronounced. This can be countered by using a slight amount of horizontal expansion. Some amount of horizontal expansion might anyway be needed if using FDM.
NOTE: This is only a scaled down dummy model of the submarine for display purposes. No working parts are present.
NOTE: Please check the terms of license before using this model.
Thank you

description_text:
The HAROP UAV is a loitering munition, or “kamikaze drone,” developed by Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI). It’s designed as a standoff, electro-optically guided attack weapon, capable of precisely targeting static or moving targets. Here’s a more detailed breakdown:
Function: The HAROP is a loitering munition, meaning it can stay airborne for extended periods, searching for and engaging targets. 
Guidance: It uses electro-optical (EO) sensors, allowing operators to select targets detected by the aircraft. 
Control: The HAROP operates using a man-in-the-loop control mode, where a remote mission operator can control the aircraft and select targets. Endurance and Range: It has an endurance of over 6 hours of flight and a range of 200 km. 
Evolution: The HAROP evolved from the HARPY, which used a Radio Frequency (RF) seeker, whereas the HAROP uses an electro-optical sensor. 
Operator Countries: The HAROP is used by several nations’ Air Forces.

The legendary PV3S is an all-terrain multi-purpose truck, (produced between 1953 and 1990) originally designed for the Czechoslovak armed forces, was a durable, popular and extremely adaptable truck built in various versions and was widely exported (72 countries). 7 Audio tracks
1 preview scene with related utility files

description_text:
What is this asset about?
If you like Advance Wars then you might like fiddling around with the land units from Advance Wars DS. The designs are referenced from the Boardgame perspective of the game by Nintendo.
I decided to upload the .blend file so users can export the asset they need to their preferred game engine but, if you're using Blender, then this might be even better for you.
Download includes:

  - Original .blend file.

  - OBJ file with all the units, though it has no animation data.

  - FBX file of all the land units but only of the Orange Star Army (file includes animations).

  - Original .afphoto file and a .psd file for better editing (also compatible with my Free Terrain Tiles pack).

  - Exporting instructions from Blender to FBX are included inside the Texture Atlas (which can be removed if needed)

Additional information for these assets:

  - The Blender file includes the original 5 armies from Nintendo as well as the 15 armies found in AWBW.

  - This asset includes a generic Infantry and Mech model based on the Orange Star Army for all the other armies. No special designs are included for the time being.

  - All units have minimum 3 animations, Idle, Select and Attack. Only the Anti Air, the APC have a different set of animations.

  - The Blender file includes the separate rocket from the Rockets unit and the separate missile form the Missile unit. Both assets have a non animated version and an animated version (for when the rockets or missiles impact their target).The animations of these assets are known to NOT WORK correctly inside Unity, but I won't be fixing this issue any time soon.

  - Except for the mentioned above, all animations have been tested in Unity and thus, should work fine on any other 3D program or Game Engine.

  - Texture Atlas is a 4K size.

  - Documentation inside files.

  - Units might need to be exported one by one for FBX purposes, so I included an export guideline in the Atlas texture with settings I KNOW WORK for Unity, so I suggest you take a peek on these before exporting anything.

  - All these assets work perfectly with my  Free 3D Terrain Tiles Advance Wars, available in this account as well. Even the texture Atlas is the same for both assets.

Awesome Extra !!!
If you'd like to have a terrain tile or a specific unit from your imagination that works with these assets, you can request them at my successfully funded Kickstarter campaign or simply send me a DM here or press the Hire Me button.

Description:The Magic Tower is a monument to forgotten times, standing tall above valleys and forests like a bridge between worlds. Built of stone that glimmers under starlight, it has witnessed countless generations pass by. Some call it a sanctuary of wisdom, others a prison of dark forces sealed away by ancient mages. At night, its top shines like a lighthouse, guiding travelers and daring adventurers toward the unknown.Many stories surround The Magic Tower, but none agree on its true purpose. Some travelers claim they heard celestial music flowing from its highest chamber, while others speak of doors that lead to entire new worlds hidden inside. Ancient runes carved into its walls seem to change with every sunrise, as if the tower itself is alive and writing its own destiny.
Scholars believe it was not built, but summoned — a creation of pure magic anchored into stone. The closer one gets, the more reality feels fragile: time slows, the air hums, and the boundary between dream and truth begins to blur. For every adventurer who dares to step inside, the tower becomes something different — a reflection of their deepest fears and their greatest desires.
To enter The Magic Tower is to gamble with fate itself. But for those who succeed in unlocking its mysteries, legends say that immortality, infinite wisdom, or a wish beyond imagination awaits at the very top.

description_text:
This is the instruction booklet to make a radio controlled model of the iconic Type 42 destroyer operated by the Royal Navy from 1975 through to 2013.  
These Type 42 destroyers were used during the Falklands War,  HMS Sheffield herself was destroyed and sunk by an Argetine Exocet missile on the 4th May 1982.
The booklet contains 30 pages of detailed instructions that is offered here free so that you can understand the process of building the model before purchasing the stl files on cgtrader.
The model is designed to be built at a scale of 1/72nd creating a model that is 1720mm long, 200mm wide and 500mm tall.
It is a model that sails extremely well, and will turn heads at a model boating pond.  
The set of stl files will complete the whole model that you see in the photographs.  The only extras you will need are motors, propellor shafts and rudders.  All hull, superstructure, fittings including railings are part of this comprehensive kit.
Enjoy the build!
Here is a link the stl files available on cgtrader   https://www.cgtrader.com/3d-print-models/hobby-diy/robotics/hms-sheffield-type-42-destroyer-radio-controlled-model

Full Description
This 3D model features a deteriorated single-engine propeller aircraft overtaken by natural overgrowth, designed for post-apocalyptic, abandoned, survival, and environmental storytelling scenes. The aircraft combines realistic structural damage with creeping vegetation to create a visually striking balance between industrial decay and nature reclaiming machinery.
The design presents a compact low-wing aircraft form with a streamlined fuselage, rear tail stabilizer, and front-mounted propeller system. The canopy and body panels are partially broken and eroded, exposing interior cavities and structural gaps that reinforce the abandoned aesthetic. Ivy vines and hanging roots spread organically across the fuselage, wings, engine section, and cockpit area, adding layered realism and natural asymmetry.
The style leans heavily into cinematic decay and atmospheric realism, suitable for dystopian environments, overgrown ruins, abandoned airfields, survival games, cinematic animations, and photorealistic renders. Surface treatment emphasizes aged metal and oxidized textures with accumulated dirt, dust, corrosion, and faded paint remnants.
Materials include weathered metal, aged painted surfaces, oxidized structural panels, broken glass elements, and dense organic vegetation. The vegetation system blends green ivy leaves with tangled dry roots and vines to create strong visual contrast against the muted aircraft body.
The color palette consists primarily of dusty beige, faded rust, oxidized brown, sand tones, muted copper, and natural green vegetation accents. Subtle surface variation and dirt buildup provide additional realism and depth under different lighting conditions.
This asset is ideal for:

  - Post-apocalyptic environments

  - Abandoned military or civilian airfields

  - Nature-reclaimed scenes

  - Survival and exploration games

  - Cinematic renders and animations

  - Environmental storytelling compositions

  - Unreal Engine and Unity projects

description_text:
1/900th scale B-Mitchell Bomber model. Certain elements not to scale.
The North American B-25 Mitchell was a twin-engine American medium bomber built from 1940–1945, with 9,816 produced and used by the United States and many Allied air forces in every theater of World War II. Armament varied heavily by model: early aircraft carried defensive machine guns and bomb loads, while later variants mounted combinations of .50 caliber machine guns, rockets, torpedoes, and even a 75 mm cannon in the B-25G and B-25H gunship versions; some late strafing versions carried up to 14 forward-firing .50 caliber machine guns. The B-25 became famous as the aircraft used in the Doolittle Raid, where 16 bombers took off from an aircraft carrier despite not being designed for carrier operations.
This model is designed and tested at 1/900th scale, but up-scaling and down-scaling are possible. Since the model is optimized for 1/900th scale, it is not ideal to print larger versions due to a lack of detail. The model has been enlarged along the z axis to allow for better printing and accentuation of detail.
